/-!
# Nonvanishing of the fixed corrected source's entire residual

The full corrected source has a nonzero closed-cell value strictly below the
cutoff transition, where its retained forcing vanishes. Continuity and actual
Hilbert representatives therefore rule out scalar proportionality of forcing
and source, and hence every native eigen-equation for this source. The exact
entire spectral-fibre classification then proves that its entire residual,
including its actual unit normalization, never vanishes at any Xi copy.

This excludes exact occurrence from this fixed corrected source. It does not
exclude other vectors, approximate source families, or the SQB interface.
-/

open Set Filter Topology MeasureTheory UpperHalfPlane ModularGroup
open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry
open scoped MatrixGroups ContDiff
namespace RHTower.SelbergScatteringSourceNonvanishing
open D4BMModularCore D4BMGlobalAngularResponse D4BMAngularSeries D4BMJointSource
open SelbergScatteringCuspSubtraction SelbergScatteringSourceVector SelbergScatteringSourceGraph
open SelbergScatteringNativeResidual
noncomputable section

/-- The original corrected source is nonzero on the closed cell strictly below
the transition forcing, retaining the complete original scalar field there. -/
theorem globalResidual_nonzero_below_transition (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    ∃ z : UpperHalfPlane, z ∈ fd ∧ z.im<2 ∧ globalResidual q z≠0 := by
  obtain ⟨x,hx⟩ := SelbergScatteringHeightConjugation.scalarSource_xi_nonzero_on_every_height q (3/2) (by norm_num)
  let z : UpperHalfPlane := ⟨⟨x,3/2⟩,by norm_num⟩
  obtain ⟨A,hA⟩ := exists_smul_mem_fd z
  have hy := modular_orbit_height_le (QuotientGroup.mk A) z
  simp only [PSL2Z_mk_smul] at hy
  have hlow : (A • z).im<2 := by
    change (A • z).im ≤ max (3/2:ℝ) (1/(3/2:ℝ)) at hy
    exact lt_of_le_of_lt hy (by norm_num)
  refine ⟨A • z,hA,hlow,?_⟩
  rw [globalResidual_eq_on_fd q _ hA,residual_low q _ hlow.le,physicalScalar_modular]
  exact hx

private theorem forcing_continuous (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    Continuous (fun z : UpperHalfPlane => cutoffForcing q (coordinates z)) := by
  have hc : Continuous coordinates := by
    apply continuous_pi
    intro i
    fin_cases i
    · exact UpperHalfPlane.continuous_re
    · exact UpperHalfPlane.continuous_im
  have h := (continuous_const (y := reflectedCompletedLambda ((q.1:ℂ)-1))).mul
    ((cutoffCommutator_continuousOn (1-(q.1:ℂ)/2)).comp_continuous hc (fun z => z.im_pos))
  apply h.congr
  intro z
  exact (SelbergScatteringCutoffForcing.cutoffForcing_eq_commutator q _ z.im_pos).symm

/-- The complete original forcing is not a scalar multiple of the original
corrected source in the native Hilbert space. -/
theorem forcingVector_ne_smul_source (q : XiZeroCopy) (c : ℂ) :
    SelbergScatteringCutoffForcing.forcingVector q ≠ c • sourceVector q := by
  intro he
  have hfield : (fun z => cutoffForcing q (coordinates z)) =ᵐ[measure]
      (fun z => c*globalResidual q z) := by
    filter_upwards [SelbergScatteringCutoffForcing.forcingVector_coe q,sourceVector_coe q,
      Lp.coeFn_smul c (sourceVector q)] with z hH hV hc
    rw [he] at hH
    simp only [Pi.smul_apply,smul_eq_mul] at hc
    rw [← hH,hc,hV]
  change (fun z => cutoffForcing q (coordinates z)) =ᵐ[volume.restrict fd]
    (fun z => c*globalResidual q z) at hfield
  have hclosure : fd ⊆ closure (interior fd) := by
    rw [← fdo_eq_interior_fd,← fd_eq_closure_fdo]
  have hpoint := Measure.eqOn_of_ae_eq hfield (forcing_continuous q).continuousOn
    (continuous_const.mul (globalResidual_smooth q).continuous).continuousOn hclosure
  obtain ⟨z,hz,hy,hn⟩ := globalResidual_nonzero_below_transition q
  have h := hpoint hz
  change cutoffForcing q (coordinates z)=c*globalResidual q z at h
  rw [cutoffForcing_low q (coordinates z) hy] at h
  have hc : c=0 := (mul_eq_zero.mp h.symm).resolve_right hn
  apply SelbergScatteringCutoffForcing.forcingVector_ne_zero q
  rw [he,hc,zero_smul]

/-- The original corrected source cannot be a native eigenvector at any complex
parameter: its retained forcing is genuinely independent of its source vector. -/
theorem sourceNativeDomain_not_eigen (q : XiZeroCopy) (lam : ℂ) :
    energyOperator (sourceNativeDomain q) ≠ lam • sourceVector q := by
  intro he
  apply forcingVector_ne_smul_source q (lam-scatteringEnergy (q.1:ℂ))
  rw [← sourceNativeDomain_equation,he,sub_smul]
  rfl

/-- The fixed complete corrected source has nonzero entire residual at every

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Suzuki.SuzukiOnePrimeTerminalForcedHardy
import Mathlib.Analysis.Fourier.LpSpace

/-!
# Canonical rough-primitive Fourier forcing for the one-prime terminal block

An `L²` physical source has a unitary vector Fourier transform.  Dividing that transform by the
derivative multiplier `2π i ξ` produces the canonical frequency forcing of its rough primitive.
Although the quotient is singular at frequency zero, multiplication by `ξ` cancels it exactly;
the origin is harmless because inverse-zero convention assigns value zero there.

This module proves the resulting first-moment bound on both frequency rays and feeds it directly
into the literal nonnormal terminal forced-Hardy theorem at Suzuki's concrete height `σ = 3/4`.
-/

open Complex MeasureTheory Set
open scoped ENNReal FourierTransform

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- A fixed normalized holomorphic square-root branch of the Gamma quotient. -/
def suzukiGammaRatioSqrtBranch : ℂ → ℂ :=
  Classical.choose GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.exists_gammaRatioSqrt

theorem suzukiGammaRatioSqrtBranch_sq
    (z : ℂ) (hz : z ∈ GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.imStrip (-1) 1) :
    suzukiGammaRatioSqrtBranch z ^ 2 = GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.gammaRatio z :=
  (Classical.choose_spec GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.exists_gammaRatioSqrt).2.1 z hz

theorem differentiableOn_suzukiGammaRatioSqrtBranch :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ suzukiGammaRatioSqrtBranch
      (GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.imStrip (-1) 1) :=
  (Classical.choose_spec GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.exists_gammaRatioSqrt).1

/-- Literal two-coordinate `L²` source space. -/
abbrev OnePrimeTerminalSourceL2 :=
  Lp (α := ℝ) OnePrimeTerminalState 2 (volume : Measure ℝ)

/-- Pointwise representative of the unitary vector Fourier transform of a terminal source. -/
def onePrimeTerminalSourceFourier (h : OnePrimeTerminalSourceL2) :
    ℝ → OnePrimeTerminalState :=
  (𝓕 h : OnePrimeTerminalSourceL2)

/-- Canonical frequency forcing of a rough primitive.  At `ξ = 0` the field inverse is zero. -/
def onePrimeTerminalRoughPrimitiveForcing (h : OnePrimeTerminalSourceL2)
    (xi : ℝ) : OnePrimeTerminalState :=
  (((2 : ℂ) * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * (xi : ℂ))⁻¹) •
    onePrimeTerminalSourceFourier h xi

theorem aestronglyMeasurable_onePrimeTerminalRoughPrimitiveForcing
    (h : OnePrimeTerminalSourceL2) :
    AEStronglyMeasurable (onePrimeTerminalRoughPrimitiveForcing h) volume := by
  change AEStronglyMeasurable (fun xi : ℝ =>
    (((2 : ℂ) * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * (xi : ℂ))⁻¹) •
      onePrimeTerminalSourceFourier h xi) volume
  have hs : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun xi : ℝ =>
      (((2 : ℂ) * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * (xi : ℂ))⁻¹)) volume :=
    (by fun_prop : Measurable fun xi : ℝ =>
      (((2 : ℂ) * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * (xi : ℂ))⁻¹)).aestronglyMeasurable
  have hf : AEStronglyMeasurable (onePrimeTerminalSourceFourier h) volume :=
    Lp.aestronglyMeasurable (𝓕 h : OnePrimeTerminalSourceL2)
  refine (hs.smul hf).congr ?_
  exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun xi => by rw [Pi.smul_apply']

/-!
# The boundary at infinity of the observer-metric space

A traceless Hermitian direction generates the ray `t ↦ exp (t T)` of observer metrics.  Two rays
are asymptotic when their distance stays bounded, and the asymptote class of a ray, based at the
reference metric, is exactly its degeneration flag:

```text
Asymptotic (ray T) (ray S)  ↔  ∀ c, eigenSum T c = eigenSum S c.
```

The forward direction is the exponential metric increasing property — distinct directions diverge
linearly, so a bounded distance forces equality — and the backward direction is that a Hermitian
direction is determined by its flag.  Since the flags are the simplices of the horizon building,
this is the card's metric-degeneration dictionary as an equivalence: the boundary point of a ray
carries exactly the information of a flag, no more and no less.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open Module

variable {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E] [FiniteDimensional ℂ E]

/-! ## Rays and the asymptote relation -/

/-- The ray of observer metrics generated by a Hermitian direction. -/
noncomputable def observerRay {T : E →ₗ[ℂ] E} (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (t : ℝ) : ObserverMetric E where
  form := (metricRay T t : E →ₗ[ℂ] E)
  isSymm := isSymmetric_metricRay hT rfl t
  isPos := fun _ hv => inner_metricRay_pos hT rfl hv t

/-- Two rays are asymptotic when the distance between them stays bounded. -/
def Asymptotic (γ δ : ℝ → ObserverMetric E) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → dist (γ t) (δ t) ≤ C

theorem asymptotic_refl (γ : ℝ → ObserverMetric E) : Asymptotic γ γ :=
  ⟨0, fun t _ => le_of_eq (dist_self (γ t))⟩

theorem Asymptotic.symm {γ δ : ℝ → ObserverMetric E} (h : Asymptotic γ δ) : Asymptotic δ γ := by
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := h
  exact ⟨C, fun t ht => by rw [dist_comm]; exact hC t ht⟩

theorem Asymptotic.trans {γ δ ε : ℝ → ObserverMetric E} (h₁ : Asymptotic γ δ)
    (h₂ : Asymptotic δ ε) : Asymptotic γ ε := by
  obtain ⟨C₁, hC₁⟩ := h₁
  obtain ⟨C₂, hC₂⟩ := h₂
  exact ⟨C₁ + C₂, fun t ht =>
    le_trans (dist_triangle (γ t) (δ t) (ε t)) (add_le_add (hC₁ t ht) (hC₂ t ht))⟩

theorem dist_observerRay {T S : E →ₗ[ℂ] E} (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric) (t : ℝ) :
    dist (observerRay hT t) (observerRay hS t)
      = observerDist (isSymmetric_metricRay hT rfl t) rfl (isSymmetric_metricRay hS rfl t) :=
  rfl

/-! ## Distinct traceless directions are not asymptotic -/

/-- **Rays with distinct traceless directions are not asymptotic.**  Their distance grows at least
linearly, by the exponential metric increasing property. -/
theorem not_asymptotic_observerRay {T S : E →ₗ[ℂ] E} (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric)
    (htr : LinearMap.trace ℂ E (S - T) = 0) (hne : S ≠ T) :
    ¬ Asymptotic (observerRay hT) (observerRay hS) := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc, hbound⟩ := exists_pos_le_observerDist_metricRay hT hS rfl htr hne
  rintro ⟨C, hC⟩
  have ht : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (|C| + 1) / c := by positivity
  have h1 := hbound ((|C| + 1) / c) ht
  have h2 := hC ((|C| + 1) / c) ht
  rw [dist_observerRay] at h2
  have hcc : c * ((|C| + 1) / c) = |C| + 1 := by field_simp
  rw [hcc] at h1
  have : |C| + 1 ≤ C := le_trans h1 h2
  linarith [le_abs_self C]

/-! ## The asymptote class is the degeneration flag -/

/-- **The asymptote class of a ray is its degeneration flag.**  Two rays of traceless directions
are asymptotic exactly when their flags agree at every threshold.  Since the flags are the
simplices of the horizon building, the boundary point of a ray carries exactly the data of a flag.
-/
theorem asymptotic_iff_eigenSum_eq {T S : E →ₗ[ℂ] E} (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric)
    (htr : LinearMap.trace ℂ E (S - T) = 0) :
    Asymptotic (observerRay hT) (observerRay hS) ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, eigenSum T c = eigenSum S c := by
  constructor
  · intro h c
    by_cases hne : S = T
    · rw [hne]
    · exact absurd h (not_asymptotic_observerRay hT hS htr hne)
  · intro h
    have hST : S = T := eq_of_eigenSum_eq hS hT rfl fun c => (h c).symm
    subst hST
    exact asymptotic_refl _

/-- **The boundary at infinity, based at the reference metric, is faithfully labelled by
directions.**  Distinct traceless directions give distinct asymptote classes. -/
theorem eq_of_asymptotic {T S : E →ₗ[ℂ] E} (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (hS : S.IsSymmetric)
    (htr : LinearMap.trace ℂ E (S - T) = 0)
    (h : Asymptotic (observerRay hT) (observerRay hS)) : S = T := by
  by_contra hne
  exact not_asymptotic_observerRay hT hS htr hne h

/-!
# Archimedean local Stokes data versus global connection constants

The Borel transform of the factorial asymptotic expansion for the exponential integral is
`1 / (1 + ξ)`: it has one simple pole at `ξ = -1` with residue `1`.  The corresponding contour jump
is therefore the universal `2πi` residue factor.  The scaled-Gamma residue infrastructure supplies
the analogous `2πi` lattice of local Gamma poles.

Local jump/difference data cannot recover a global additive connection coefficient: adding any
constant leaves every two-point difference unchanged.  The closed noninjectivity theorem below is
the exact abstract obstruction behind the valid part of the archimedean local/global distinction.
-/

open Complex Filter Set
open scoped Topology

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- Borel transform of the factorial tail in the asymptotic expansion of `E₁`. -/
def exponentialIntegralBorel (ξ : ℂ) : ℂ := (1 + ξ)⁻¹

/-- Its denominator vanishes exactly at the single Borel singularity `-1`. -/
theorem exponentialIntegralBorel_denominator_eq_zero_iff (ξ : ℂ) :
    1 + ξ = 0 ↔ ξ = -1 := by
  constructor <;> intro h
  · linear_combination h
  · rw [h]
    ring

/-- The Borel singularity at `-1` is simple and has residue `1`. -/
theorem exponentialIntegralBorel_residue_at_neg_one :
    Tendsto
      (fun ξ : ℂ => (ξ - (-1)) * exponentialIntegralBorel ξ)
      (nhdsWithin (-1) ({(-1 : ℂ)}ᶜ)) (nhds 1) := by
  let denominator : ℂ → ℂ := fun ξ => ξ + 1
  let numerator : ℂ → ℂ := fun _ => 1
  have hden : HasDerivAt denominator 1 (-1) := by
    simpa [denominator] using (hasDerivAt_id (-1)).add_const (1 : ℂ)
  have hden0 : denominator (-1) = 0 := by simp [denominator]
  have hnum : ContinuousAt numerator (-1) := by fun_prop
  have hres := RHTower.tendsto_residue_of_simple_zero
    hden hden0 one_ne_zero hnum
  simpa [denominator, numerator, exponentialIntegralBorel, add_comm] using hres

/-- Local connection data retaining only differences between endpoint values. -/
def connectionDifferenceProfile (f : ℂ → ℂ) : ℂ × ℂ → ℂ :=
  fun zw => f zw.1 - f zw.2

/-- Adding a global connection constant changes no local difference data. -/
theorem connectionDifferenceProfile_add_const (f : ℂ → ℂ) (c : ℂ) :
    connectionDifferenceProfile (fun z => f z + c) = connectionDifferenceProfile f := by
  funext zw
  simp [connectionDifferenceProfile]

/-- **Global connection coefficients are not reconstructible from local jump data.** The zero and
one functions are distinct but have the same complete difference profile. -/
theorem connectionDifferenceProfile_not_injective :
    ¬ Function.Injective connectionDifferenceProfile := by
  intro h
  let f : ℂ → ℂ := fun _ => 0
  let g : ℂ → ℂ := fun _ => 1
  have hprofile : connectionDifferenceProfile f = connectionDifferenceProfile g := by
    funext zw
    simp [connectionDifferenceProfile, f, g]
  have hfg := h hprofile
  have hzero := congrFun hfg 0
  simp [f, g] at hzero

/-- Closed local/global endpoint for the exponential-integral seam. -/
theorem archimedeanLocalGlobalRegulatorBoundary :
    Tendsto
      (fun ξ : ℂ => (ξ - (-1)) * exponentialIntegralBorel ξ)
      (nhdsWithin (-1) ({(-1 : ℂ)}ᶜ)) (nhds 1) ∧
    ¬ Function.Injective connectionDifferenceProfile :=
  ⟨exponentialIntegralBorel_residue_at_neg_one,
    connectionDifferenceProfile_not_injective⟩

end
end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

ow_eq {ι : Type*} (omega : ι → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    circlePhaseFlow omega t
      = unitTorusHomeomorphCircles ι (HTGeometry.clockPhasePoint omega t) := rfl

/-- **Forward tails of the circle phase flow are dense.** -/
theorem dense_forwardOrbit_circlePhaseFlow {ι : Type*} [Countable ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {omega : ι → ℝ} (hindep : HTGeometry.RationallyIndependentSequence omega) (T₀ : ℝ) :
    Dense {x : ι → Circle | ∃ t : ℝ, T₀ ≤ t ∧ circlePhaseFlow omega t = x} := by
  have hbase := HTGeometry.dense_forwardOrbit hindep T₀
  have himage : (unitTorusHomeomorphCircles ι) ''
      {x : UnitAddTorus ι | ∃ t : ℝ, T₀ ≤ t ∧ HTGeometry.clockPhasePoint omega t = x}
      ⊆ {x : ι → Circle | ∃ t : ℝ, T₀ ≤ t ∧ circlePhaseFlow omega t = x} := by
    rintro - ⟨y, ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨t, ht, (circlePhaseFlow_eq omega t)⟩
  refine Dense.mono himage ?_
  exact (unitTorusHomeomorphCircles ι).surjective.denseRange.dense_image
    (unitTorusHomeomorphCircles ι).continuous hbase

/-- **The orbit closure of an asymptotic Bohr orbit.**  For an exponential carrier with summable
weights and rationally independent frequencies, an orbit asymptotic to the phase hull along the
phase flow has closure exactly the orbit together with the whole hull, a homeomorphic copy of the
phase torus. -/
theorem bohrHull_closure_range_eq {ι : Type*} [Countable ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {a : ι → ℂ} {omega : ι → ℝ} (h : ExpSeriesNormallySummable a omega)
    (hindep : HTGeometry.RationallyIndependentSequence omega)
    {G : ℝ → C(ℂ, ℂ)} (hG : Continuous G)
    (hasym : Tendsto (fun t => (bohrHullMap a omega h (circlePhaseFlow omega t), G t))
      (Filter.cocompact ℝ) (uniformity C(ℂ, ℂ))) :
    closure (Set.range G) = Set.range G ∪ Set.range (bohrHullMap a omega h) :=
  closure_range_eq_union_range (continuous_bohrHullMap h) hG
    (dense_forwardOrbit_circlePhaseFlow hindep) hasym

end

/-!
# Boundary points are limits of the orbit

An orbit which is asymptotic to a continuous parametrised family along a flow with dense forward
tails accumulates on the whole family: to reach a prescribed parameter one waits until the orbit is
close to the family, and then uses density of the remaining tail to steer the flow near that
parameter.

For the hull of an exponential carrier this says that every boundary state is a limit of orbit
states, which is the inclusion `B ⊆ closure O` of the orbit closure decomposition.
-/

open Filter Topology Set

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

noncomputable section

/-- **Asymptotic orbits reach every parameter.**  If a family `α` is continuous, the flow `θ` has
dense forward tails, and the orbit `G` is asymptotic to `α ∘ θ`, then every value of `α` lies in the
closure of the orbit. -/
theorem mem_closure_range_of_dense_tails {T Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace T] [UniformSpace Y]
    {α : T → Y} {θ : ℝ → T} {G : ℝ → Y} (hα : Continuous α)
    (htails : ∀ T₀ : ℝ, Dense {x : T | ∃ t : ℝ, T₀ ≤ t ∧ θ t = x})
    (hasym : ∀ V ∈ uniformity Y, ∀ᶠ t in atTop, (α (θ t), G t) ∈ V)
    (x : T) : α x ∈ closure (Set.range G) := by
  rw [mem_closure_iff_nhds]
  intro N hN
  obtain ⟨V, hV, hVN⟩ := UniformSpace.mem_nhds_iff.mp hN
  obtain ⟨W, hW, hWV⟩ := comp_mem_uniformity_sets hV
  have hpre : α ⁻¹' (UniformSpace.ball (α x) W) ∈ 𝓝 x :=
    hα.continuousAt (UniformSpace.ball_mem_nhds _ hW)
  obtain ⟨T₀, hT₀⟩ := Filter.eventually_atTop.mp (hasym W hW)
  set U : Set T := interior (α ⁻¹' UniformSpace.ball (α x) W) with hU
  have hUopen : IsOpen U := isOpen_interior
  have hxU : x ∈ U := mem_interior_iff_mem_nhds.mpr hpre
  obtain ⟨y, hyU, hyorbit⟩ :=
    (dense_iff_inter_open.mp (htails T₀)) U hUopen ⟨x, hxU⟩
  obtain ⟨t, htT₀, rfl⟩ := hyorbit
  rw [hU] at hyU
  have hmem : θ t ∈ α ⁻¹' UniformSpace.ball (α x) W := interior_subset hyU
  have hball : α (θ t) ∈ UniformSpace.ball (α x) W := hmem
  have hGt : (α x, G t) ∈ V := by
    refine hWV ?_
    exact ⟨α (θ t), hball, hT₀ t htT₀⟩
  refine ⟨G t, hVN hGt, ⟨t, rfl⟩⟩

/-- **Every boundary state of the hull is a limit of an asymptotic orbit.**  Specialised to the
phase hull of an exponential carrier: the phase flow has dense forward tails, so an orbit asymptotic
to the boundary family accumulates on the whole boundary. -/
theorem bohrHullMap_mem_closure_range_of_asymptotic {ι : Type*} [Countable ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    {a : ι → ℂ} {omega : ι → ℝ} (h : ExpSeriesNormallySummable a omega)
    {phase : ℝ → ι → Circle} {G : ℝ → C(ℂ, ℂ)}
    (hflow : ∀ T₀ : ℝ, Dense {x : ι → Circle | ∃ t : ℝ, T₀ ≤ t ∧ phase t = x})
    (hasym : ∀ V ∈ uniformity C(ℂ, ℂ), ∀ᶠ t in atTop,
      (bohrHullMap a omega h (phase t), G t) ∈ V)
    (lam : ι → Circle) :
    bohrHullMap a omega h lam ∈ closure (Set.range G) :=
  mem_closure_range_of_dense_tails (continuous_bohrHullMap h) hflow hasym lam


/-! ## Splitting the closure of an orbit -/

/-- **Bounded times contribute only orbit points.**  The image of a compact time window is closed,
so a limit of orbit points from a bounded window is itself an orbit point. -/
theorem mem_range_of_mem_closure_image_compact {Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y]
    {G : ℝ → Y} (hG : Continuous G) {M : ℝ} {y : Y}
    (hy : y ∈ closure (G '' Set.Icc (-M) M)) : y ∈ Set.range G := by
  have hcompact : IsCompact (G '' Set.Icc (-M) M) := (isCompact_Icc).image hG
  have hclosed : IsClosed (G '' Set.Icc (-M) M) := hcompact.isClosed
  rw [hclosed.closure_eq] at hy
  obtain ⟨t, -, rfl⟩ := hy
  exact ⟨t, rfl⟩

/-- **The closure of an orbit splits.**  A limit of orbit points is either an orbit point or a
cluster point of the orbit at arbitrarily large times. -/
theorem closure_range_subset_union_clusterAtInfinity {Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y]
    {G : ℝ → Y} (hG : Continuous G) :
    closure (Set.range G) ⊆ Set.range G ∪ ⋂ M : ℝ, closure (G '' {t : ℝ | M < |t|}) := by
  intro y hy
  by_cases hrange : y ∈ Set.range G
  · exact Or.inl hrange
  refine Or.inr (Set.mem_iInter.mpr fun M => ?_)
  have hsplit : Set.range G = G '' Set.Icc (-M) M ∪ G '' {t : ℝ | M < |t|} := by
    rw [← Set.image_union]
    have hcover : Set.Icc (-M) M ∪ {t : ℝ | M < |t|} = Set.univ := by
      ext t
      simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_Icc, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_univ, iff_true]
      rcases le_or_gt |t| M with habs | habs
      · exact Or.inl ⟨by cases abs_le.mp habs with | intro h1 h2 => linarith,
          (abs_le.mp habs).2⟩
      · exact Or.inr habs
    rw [hcover, Set.image_univ]
  rw [hsplit, closure_union] at hy
  rcases hy with hy | hy
  · exact absurd (mem_range_of_mem_closure_image_compact hG hy) hrange
  · exact hy

/-!
# Rational functions cannot decay exponentially on a real ray

The ray-complete translation theorem first shows that a translated generalized Dirichlet carrier
decays exponentially on the positive real axis.  This file supplies the exact missing separation:
a quotient of two complex polynomials with nonzero numerator and denominator is asymptotic to a
nonzero integral power, and therefore cannot be `O(exp (-eta*x))` for `eta > 0`.
-/

open Filter Topology Asymptotics Polynomial Bornology

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

/-- A quotient of nonzero complex polynomials is asymptotic on the positive real axis to the
quotient of leading coefficients times the corresponding integral power. -/
theorem complexPolynomial_div_isEquivalent_atTop
    {p q : Polynomial ℂ} (hp : p ≠ 0) (hq : q ≠ 0) :
    (fun x : ℝ => p.eval (x : ℂ) / q.eval (x : ℂ)) ~[atTop]
      (fun x : ℝ => (p.leadingCoeff / q.leadingCoeff) *
        (x : ℂ) ^ ((p.natDegree : ℤ) - q.natDegree)) := by
  have hpEq : (fun x : ℝ => p.eval (x : ℂ)) ~[atTop]
      (fun x : ℝ => p.leadingCoeff * (x : ℂ) ^ p.natDegree) := by
    simpa [Function.comp_def] using
      (Polynomial.isEquivalent_cobounded_leading_monomial (P := p)).comp_tendsto
        (RCLike.tendsto_ofReal_atTop_cobounded ℂ)
  have hqEq : (fun x : ℝ => q.eval (x : ℂ)) ~[atTop]
      (fun x : ℝ => q.leadingCoeff * (x : ℂ) ^ q.natDegree) := by
    simpa [Function.comp_def] using
      (Polynomial.isEquivalent_cobounded_leading_monomial (P := q)).comp_tendsto
        (RCLike.tendsto_ofReal_atTop_cobounded ℂ)
  refine (hpEq.div hqEq).trans (EventuallyEq.isEquivalent ?_)
  filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop (0 : ℝ)] with x hx
  have hxC : (x : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hx.ne'
  have hpLC : p.leadingCoeff ≠ 0 := Polynomial.leadingCoeff_ne_zero.mpr hp
  have hqLC : q.leadingCoeff ≠ 0 := Polynomial.leadingCoeff_ne_zero.mpr hq
  change (p.leadingCoeff * (x : ℂ) ^ p.natDegree) /
      (q.leadingCoeff * (x : ℂ) ^ q.natDegree) = _
  rw [zpow_sub₀ hxC]
  field_simp
  simp only [zpow_natCast]
  ring

/-- A negative exponential is little-o of every integral power along the positive real axis. -/
theorem complex_exp_neg_isLittleO_zpow_atTop {eta : ℝ} (heta : 0 < eta) (d : ℤ) :
    (fun x : ℝ => (Real.exp (-eta * x) : ℂ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun x : ℝ => (x : ℂ) ^ d) := by
  apply IsLittleO.of_norm_norm
  have h := isLittleO_exp_neg_mul_rpow_atTop heta (d : ℝ)
  apply h.congr'
  · filter_upwards with x
    rw [Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (Real.exp_pos _)]
  · filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop (0 : ℝ)] with x hx
    rw [norm_zpow, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos hx,
      ← Real.rpow_intCast]

/-- A nonzero rational polynomial quotient cannot be bounded by a strictly decaying exponential. -/
theorem complexPolynomial_div_not_isBigO_exp_neg
    {p q : Polynomial ℂ} (hp : p ≠ 0) (hq : q ≠ 0)
    {eta : ℝ} (heta : 0 < eta) :
    ¬ (fun x : ℝ => p.eval (x : ℂ) / q.eval (x : ℂ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun x : ℝ => (Real.exp (-eta * x) : ℂ)) := by
  intro hO
  let d : ℤ := (p.natDegree : ℤ) - q.natDegree
  let c : ℂ := p.leadingCoeff / q.leadingCoeff
  have hc : c ≠ 0 := div_ne_zero
    (Polynomial.leadingCoeff_ne_zero.mpr hp) (Polynomial.leadingCoeff_ne_zero.mpr hq)
  have heq : (fun x : ℝ => p.eval (x : ℂ) / q.eval (x : ℂ)) ~[atTop]
      (fun x : ℝ => c * (x : ℂ) ^ d) := by
    simpa [c, d] using complexPolynomial_div_isEquivalent_atTop hp hq
  have hexp : (fun x : ℝ => (Real.exp (-eta * x) : ℂ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun x : ℝ => c * (x : ℂ) ^ d) :=
    (complex_exp_neg_isLittleO_zpow_atTop heta d).const_mul_right hc

    heq.symm.trans_isLittleO (hO.trans_isLittleO hexp)
  apply (isLittleO_irrefl ?_) hself
  exact Filter.Eventually.frequently <|
    (eventually_gt_atTop (0 : ℝ)).mono fun x hx =>
      mul_ne_zero hc (zpow_ne_zero _ (by exact_mod_cast hx.ne'))

/-- Pointwise exponential domination on a tail forces the numerator of a polynomial quotient to
vanish. -/
theorem complexPolynomial_eq_zero_of_div_exponential_bound
    {p q : Polynomial ℂ} (hq : q ≠ 0) {eta C : ℝ} (heta : 0 < eta) (_hC : 0 ≤ C)
    (hbound : ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop,
      ‖p.eval (x : ℂ) / q.eval (x : ℂ)‖ ≤ C * Real.exp (-eta * x)) :
    p = 0 := by
  by_contra hp
  apply complexPolynomial_div_not_isBigO_exp_neg hp hq heta
  apply IsBigO.of_bound C
  filter_upwards [hbound] with x hx
  simpa [Complex.norm_exp] using hx

source_arguments.statement:
private theorem moebiusLogHarmonicPartial_eq_abel (N : ℕ) :
    moebiusLogHarmonicPartial N =
      RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial N * (-Real.log (N : ℝ)) +
        ∑ i ∈ Finset.range N, RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial i *
          (Real.log ((i : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (i : ℝ))
source_arguments.source_statement:
private theorem moebiusLogHarmonicPartial_eq_abel (N : ℕ) :
    moebiusLogHarmonicPartial N =
      RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial N * (-Real.log (N : ℝ)) +
        ∑ i ∈ Finset.range N, RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial i *
          (Real.log ((i : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (i : ℝ))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have habel := RHTower.deningerAbelSummation
    (fun n : ℕ => ((moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ))
    (fun n : ℕ => -Real.log (n : ℝ)) N
  have hpartial : RHTower.deningerPartialSum
      (fun n : ℕ => ((moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)) N =
    RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial N := by rfl
  rw [hpartial] at habel
  rw [moebiusLogHarmonicPartial]
  calc
    ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), moebiusLogHarmonicTerm n =
        ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1),
          ((moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) * -Real.log (n : ℝ) := by
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun n hn => ?_
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hn0
      · simp [moebiusLogHarmonicTerm]
      · have hnr : (0 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn0
        rw [moebiusLogHarmonicTerm, Real.rpow_neg_one]
        field_simp
    _ = RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial N * (-Real.log (N : ℝ)) +
        ∑ i ∈ Finset.range N, RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial i *
          (-Real.log (i : ℝ) - -Real.log ((i + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) := habel
    _ = RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial N * (-Real.log (N : ℝ)) +
        ∑ i ∈ Finset.range N, RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial i *
          (Real.log ((i : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (i : ℝ)) := by
      congr 1
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i hi => ?_
      push_cast
      ring

# Möbius logarithmic jets preserve hypertranscendence; Li coefficients are not holonomic

- **ID:** `mobius-logarithmic-jet-ht-transfer-li-no-holonomic-route`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper) / route no-go
- **Scientific status:** `[PROVED HERE] [UNCONDITIONAL] [BRIDGE] [NOT NEW SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE]`
- **Lane:** general hypertranscendence; coefficient transforms; Li-criterion boundary
- **Statement:** For a nonzero meromorphic function, logarithmic differentiation after a Möbius
  change preserves DA versus HT exactly.  Independently, a function with infinitely many zeros has
  a non-D-finite Möbius logarithmic jet.  Consequently the Li sequence is unconditionally not
  P-recursive, and no holonomic closed-recurrence implementation of Li's criterion can prove RH.
  The independently proved augmentation-exposure theorem makes completed `xi` HT, so its Li
  generator is unconditionally HT as well.

## Goal

Find an exact point at which hypertranscendence excludes a literature route rather than merely
making it difficult.  Li's criterion itself is equivalent to RH and cannot honestly be declared
incapable of proving RH.  The theorem instead isolates and kills a concrete implementation found in
the Li literature: close the Li coefficients under a finite linear recurrence with polynomial
coefficients and prove positivity inductively.

The no-go is deliberately limited to a **closed holonomic recurrence**.  Recurrences with a new
zero-sum forcing term at every index, integral/norm representations, Weil positivity, and genuinely
infinite-dimensional arguments remain possible.

## General transfer theorem `[PROVED HERE]`

Let `K=C(z)`, let `F` be a nonzero meromorphic function, and let

`r(z)=(az+b)/(cz+d)`, `ad-bc != 0`,

be a nonconstant Möbius transformation with rational inverse `q`.  Define the Möbius logarithmic
jet

`J_r(F)(z)=r'(z) F'(r(z))/F(r(z))`.

Then

`F is DA over C(z) iff J_r(F) is DA over C(z)`.

Equivalently,

`F is HT over C(z) iff J_r(F) is HT over C(z)`.

On every simply connected zero-free germ on which a logarithm is chosen, these are also equivalent
to differential algebraicity or hypertranscendence of `log(F o r)`.

### Forward implication

If `F` is DA, so are `F'`, `1/F`, and `F'/F`.  The DA meromorphic functions form a differential
field and are closed under composition with a rational function.  Multiplication by the rational
function `r'` shows that `J_r(F)` is DA.

### Reverse implication

Suppose `J_r(F)` is DA.  Substitute `z=q(w)`.  Since `q` is rational and

`r'(q(w)) q'(w)=1`,

one obtains

`F'(w)/F(w)=q'(w) J_r(F)(q(w))`.

The right side is DA.  Thus `F` solves the first-order linear equation

`Y' = u Y`, `u=F'/F`,

over a DA differential extension of `C(w)`.  Hence `F` is DA over that extension, and transitivity
of differential algebraicity makes `F` DA over `C(w)`.

For a local logarithm `G=log(F o r)`, one has `G'=J_r(F)`.  Differentiation preserves DA, while an
ADE for `G'` becomes an ADE for `G` after shifting every derivative index by one.  Therefore `G` is
DA exactly when `J_r(F)` is DA.  This completes all equivalences.  ∎

## Li specialization `[PROVED HERE, UNCONDITIONAL]`

Let `xi` be Riemann's completed xi-function and put

`r(z)=1/(1-z)`, `q(w)=1-1/w`.

Near `z=0`, the Keiper--Li generating identity is

`log xi(1/(1-z)) = log xi(1) + sum_(n>=1) (lambda_n/n) z^n`.

Consequently

`L_Li(z):=sum_(n>=1) lambda_n z^(n-1)`

`=d/dz log xi(1/(1-z))`

`=(1-z)^(-2) xi'(1/(1-z))/xi(1/(1-z))`

`=J_r(xi)(z)`.

The completed-logarithmic-derivative augmentation theorem proves unconditionally that `xi'/xi` is
HT over `C(s)`: applying the shift `s -> s+2` strips the common gamma mode and exposes an ordinary
Dirichlet series with nonzero coefficients at every prime, to which Ostrowski applies.  The
logarithmic-derivative equivalence then makes `xi` HT.  Applying the transfer theorem gives

`L_Li is HT over C(z)`.

The integrated Keiper--Li series `sum lambda_n z^n/n` is HT as well.

## Infinite-divisor obstruction to holonomicity `[PROVED HERE]`

Let `F` be a nonzero entire function with infinitely many distinct zeros, and let `r` be a Möbius
transformation.  Then `J_r(F)` is not D-finite over `C(z)`.

Indeed, `F'/F` has a pole at every zero of `F`, with residue equal to its positive multiplicity.
Möbius transformations are injective and have nonvanishing derivative away from their single pole,
so `J_r(F)` has poles at infinitely many distinct finite inverse images of zeros of `F` (discarding
at most the one zero mapped to infinity).

By contrast, an analytic germ satisfying a linear differential equation with polynomial
coefficients can have finite-plane singularities only among the finitely many zeros of the leading
coefficient.  It analytically continues along every path avoiding that finite set.  Therefore a
D-finite germ cannot have infinitely many distinct finite poles.  Hence `J_r(F)` is not D-finite. ∎

The tree owns the exact Möbius inversion of the polar unit,
`∑_{d ≤ N} μ(d) H_{⌊N/d⌋}/d = 1`.  Replacing the harmonic floor by its logarithm turns it into an
exact identity for the logarithmic Möbius sum, with the whole remaining content isolated in the
error sum `∑_{d ≤ N} (μ(d)/d)(H_{⌊N/d⌋} − log(N/d))`.  This is the last elementary step of Graham's
evaluation.

open Finset ArithmeticFunction
open scoped ArithmeticFunction.Moebius BigOperators

namespace RHTower.Sieve

theorem harmonicFloorMoebiusSum_eq_one_real (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    (∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
        ((μ d : ℤ) : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) * ((harmonic (N / d) : ℚ) : ℝ)) = 1 := by
  have h := RHTower.harmonicFloorMoebiusSum_eq_one N hN
  have hcast : ((∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      ((μ d : ℤ) : ℚ) / (d : ℚ) * harmonic (N / d) : ℚ) : ℝ)
      = ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
        ((μ d : ℤ) : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) * ((harmonic (N / d) : ℚ) : ℝ) := by
    push_cast
    ring
  rw [← hcast, h]
  norm_num

/-- **The logarithmic Möbius sum, exactly.**  The whole content is the harmonic-versus-logarithm
error sum. -/
theorem sum_moebius_log_div_eq_one_sub_error (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    (∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ((μ d : ℤ) : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) * Real.log ((N : ℝ) / (d : ℝ)))

          (((harmonic (N / d) : ℚ) : ℝ) - Real.log ((N : ℝ) / (d : ℝ))) := by
  have hbase := harmonicFloorMoebiusSum_eq_one_real N hN
  have hsplit : (∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ((μ d : ℤ) : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) *
        (((harmonic (N / d) : ℚ) : ℝ) - Real.log ((N : ℝ) / (d : ℝ))))

    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]

# Affine shifts of the real-cutoff logarithmic Möbius kernels

Layer-cake truncation replaces `log(X/d)` by `t + log(Y/d)`, where `Y = X exp(-t)`.
The linear and quadratic shifted sums below reduce exactly to the existing unshifted kernels and
the Möbius harmonic boundary.  No new analytic estimate is introduced.

open Finset ArithmeticFunction
open scoped ArithmeticFunction.Moebius BigOperators

namespace RHTower.Sieve

noncomputable section

/-- Linear logarithmic Möbius kernel after an affine logarithmic shift. -/
def moebiusShiftedLogKernelReal (t Y : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 ⌊Y⌋₊,
    ((moebius d : ℤ) : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) *
      (t + Real.log (Y / (d : ℝ)))

/-- Quadratic logarithmic Möbius kernel after an affine logarithmic shift. -/
def moebiusShiftedLogSqKernelReal (t Y : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 ⌊Y⌋₊,
    ((moebius d : ℤ) : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) *
      (t + Real.log (Y / (d : ℝ))) ^ 2

/-- Exact affine-shift identity for the linear logarithmic Möbius kernel. -/
theorem moebiusShiftedLogKernelReal_eq
    (t Y : ℝ) :
    moebiusShiftedLogKernelReal t Y =
      coprimeLogMoebius 1 Y +
        t * RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial ⌊Y⌋₊ := by
  have hpartial : RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial ⌊Y⌋₊ =
      ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 ⌊Y⌋₊,
        ((moebius d : ℤ) : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) := by
    rw [RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial, Finset.sum_range_succ']
    simp
    convert RHTower.sum_range_succ_eq_sum_Icc
      (fun d : ℕ => ((moebius d : ℤ) : ℝ) / (d : ℝ)) ⌊Y⌋₊ using 1
    all_goals push_cast
    all_goals ring
  rw [moebiusShiftedLogKernelReal, coprimeLogMoebius,
    Finset.filter_true_of_mem (fun d _ => Nat.coprime_one_left d),
    hpartial, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro d hd
  ring

/-- Exact affine-shift identity for the quadratic logarithmic Möbius kernel. -/
theorem moebiusShiftedLogSqKernelReal_eq
    (t Y : ℝ) :
    moebiusShiftedLogSqKernelReal t Y =
      moebiusDoubleLogKernelReal Y + 2 * t * coprimeLogMoebius 1 Y +
        t ^ 2 * RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial ⌊Y⌋₊ := by
  have hpartial : RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial ⌊Y⌋₊ =
      ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 ⌊Y⌋₊,
        ((moebius d : ℤ) : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) := by
    rw [RHTower.deningerHarmonicPartial, Finset.sum_range_succ']
    simp
    convert RHTower.sum_range_succ_eq_sum_Icc
      (fun d : ℕ => ((moebius d : ℤ) : ℝ) / (d : ℝ)) ⌊Y⌋₊ using 1
    all_goals push_cast
    all_goals ring
  rw [moebiusShiftedLogSqKernelReal, moebiusDoubleLogKernelReal,
    coprimeLogMoebius,
    Finset.filter_true_of_mem (fun d _ => Nat.coprime_one_left d),
    hpartial, Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib,
    ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro d hd
  ring

end

end RHTower.Sieve

/-!
# The finite Möbius--log divisor paraproduct

The exact convolution identity `μ * log = Λ` rewrites every finite weighted von Mangoldt sum as a
pair-labelled divisor sum.  Specializing the weight to the critical moving tent gives the precise
Möbius--logarithm paraproduct that must be retained through the prime--polar cancellation.

This file is purely finite and algebraic.  It makes no estimate on either marginal and does not
assert the still-open compensated decomposition or one-sided cutoff-commutator bound.
-/

open Nat ArithmeticFunction Finset
open scoped BigOperators Moebius

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- The pair-labelled finite divisor paraproduct associated to a weight `w`.  An index
`x ∈ k.divisorsAntidiagonal` records the ordered factorization `x.1 * x.2 = k`. -/
def mobiusLogDivisorParaproduct (w : ℕ → ℝ) (K : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 K, ∑ x ∈ k.divisorsAntidiagonal,
    (ArithmeticFunction.moebius x.1 : ℝ) * Real.log x.2 * w k

/-- **Exact finite Möbius--log rewrite.** Every finitely weighted von Mangoldt sum is the
label-retaining divisor paraproduct obtained from `μ * log = Λ`. -/
theorem weightedVonMangoldt_eq_mobiusLogDivisorParaproduct
    (w : ℕ → ℝ) (K : ℕ) :
    (∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 K, ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt k * w k) =
      mobiusLogDivisorParaproduct w K := by
  rw [mobiusLogDivisorParaproduct]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro k hk
  rw [← ArithmeticFunction.moebius_mul_log_eq_vonMangoldt]
  simp only [ArithmeticFunction.mul_apply, ArithmeticFunction.intCoe_apply,
    ArithmeticFunction.log_apply, Finset.sum_mul]

/-- The exact critical half-density paraproduct for the moving multiplicative tent. -/
def rectangularMobiusLogDivisorParaproduct (L N : ℝ) (K : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 K, ∑ x ∈ k.divisorsAntidiagonal,
    (ArithmeticFunction.moebius x.1 : ℝ) * Real.log x.2 / Real.sqrt k *
      rectangularMovingPrimeTent L N k

/-- **Critical Möbius--log divisor identity.** The complete moving von Mangoldt tent is exactly
the finite ordered-factorization paraproduct.  The equality is established before any
scalarization, so the Möbius sign, logarithmic complement, product scale, and cutoff label all
remain present. -/
theorem rectangularMovingPrimeTentSum_eq_mobiusLogDivisorParaproduct
    (L N : ℝ) (K : ℕ) :
    rectangularMovingPrimeTentSum L N K =
      rectangularMobiusLogDivisorParaproduct L N K := by
  rw [rectangularMovingPrimeTentSum,
    rectangularMobiusLogDivisorParaproduct]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro k hk
  rw [← ArithmeticFunction.moebius_mul_log_eq_vonMangoldt]
  simp only [ArithmeticFunction.mul_apply, ArithmeticFunction.intCoe_apply,
    ArithmeticFunction.log_apply, Finset.sum_div, Finset.sum_mul]

end

end RHTower

/-!
# Finite critical Möbius causal virial

This module records the exact finite algebra behind the causal-complement virial used by the
unit-Riesz Markov factorization.  It is known-derived corpus infrastructure, not new scientific
knowledge and not an RH proof.

For a finite critical Möbius boundary, subtracting `T` times the causal complement from its
primitive cancels the entire boundary mass and leaves only the logarithmic Möbius moment plus the
explicit polar term.  No estimate or zero information is used.
-/

open Nat ArithmeticFunction Finset
open scoped BigOperators Moebius

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Finite critical weighted-Möbius boundary mass. -/
def finiteCriticalMobiusBoundary (K : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K,
    ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ) / n

/-- Finite logarithmic moment of the critical weighted-Möbius boundary. -/
def finiteCriticalMobiusLogMoment (K : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K,
    (((ArithmeticFunction.moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ) / n) * Real.log n

/-- Finite critical causal complement `exp(-T)-m_K`. -/
def finiteCriticalMobiusCausalComplement (T : ℝ) (K : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  Real.exp (-T) - finiteCriticalMobiusBoundary K

/-- Exact primitive of the finite step-boundary model, written without analytic integration. -/
def finiteCriticalMobiusCausalPrimitive (T : ℝ) (K : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  1 - Real.exp (-T) -
    ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K,
      (((ArithmeticFunction.moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ) / n) * (T - Real.log n)

/-- Causal virial `primitive - T * complement`. -/
def finiteCriticalMobiusCausalVirial (T : ℝ) (K : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  finiteCriticalMobiusCausalPrimitive T K -
    T * finiteCriticalMobiusCausalComplement T K

/-- **Finite causal-virial collapse.**  Boundary mass cancels exactly, leaving the logarithmic
Möbius moment and explicit polar correction. -/
theorem finiteCriticalMobiusCausalVirial_eq_logMoment
    (T : ℝ) (K : ℕ) :
    finiteCriticalMobiusCausalVirial T K =
      1 - (1 + T) * Real.exp (-T) + finiteCriticalMobiusLogMoment K := by
  rw [finiteCriticalMobiusCausalVirial, finiteCriticalMobiusCausalPrimitive,
    finiteCriticalMobiusCausalComplement, finiteCriticalMobiusBoundary,
    finiteCriticalMobiusLogMoment]
  simp_rw [mul_sub]
  rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, ← Finset.sum_mul]
  ring

/-- Sign convention matching the paper's `Q(X)=-sum mu(n)log(n)/n`. -/
def finiteCriticalMobiusLogDefect (K : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  -finiteCriticalMobiusLogMoment K

/-- Equivalent source-facing form of the finite causal virial. -/
theorem finiteCriticalMobiusCausalVirial_eq_one_sub_logDefect
    (T : ℝ) (K : ℕ) :
    finiteCriticalMobiusCausalVirial T K =
      1 - (1 + T) * Real.exp (-T) - finiteCriticalMobiusLogDefect K := by
  rw [finiteCriticalMobiusCausalVirial_eq_logMoment, finiteCriticalMobiusLogDefect]
  ring

end

end RHTower

/-!
# Bounded normal-form Hasse coordinates for compatible cyclic algebras

A compatible raw cyclic algebra has one coefficient in its defining field at each exponent below
the cyclic degree.  Existing companion faithfulness makes those bounded coordinates unique.  This
file exposes the resulting additive equivalence, unique-coordinate existence, coefficientwise
congruence, zero detection, and finite detecting witnesses.

This complements matrix-entry Hasse separation: companion entries are external representation
coordinates, while these are intrinsic cyclic-algebra coefficients.  Neither is yet the local
Brauer invariant required by full ABHN reciprocity.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ABHN
namespace CyclicCompanionDatum

universe u

variable {L : Type u} [Field L]

/-- Additive equivalence between bounded coefficient packets and a compatible cyclic algebra. -/
noncomputable def normalFormEquiv (D : CyclicCompanionDatum L) :
    (Fin (D.predDegree + 1) → L) ≃+
      CyclicAlgebra D.automorphism (D.predDegree + 1) D.parameter :=
  cyclicCompanionNormalFormAddEquiv D.automorphism D.predDegree D.parameter
    D.order_eq_one D.parameter_fixed

/-- Unique bounded coefficient profile of a compatible cyclic-algebra element. -/
noncomputable def normalFormCoordinates (D : CyclicCompanionDatum L)
    (x : CyclicAlgebra D.automorphism (D.predDegree + 1) D.parameter) :
    Fin (D.predDegree + 1) → L :=
  D.normalFormEquiv.symm x

/-- Reconstruct an element from its unique bounded coefficient profile. -/
theorem normalForm_reconstruct (D : CyclicCompanionDatum L)
    (x : CyclicAlgebra D.automorphism (D.predDegree + 1) D.parameter) :
    cyclicCompanionNormalForm D.automorphism D.predDegree D.parameter
      (D.normalFormCoordinates x) = x := by
  change D.normalFormEquiv (D.normalFormEquiv.symm x) = x
  exact D.normalFormEquiv.apply_symm_apply x

/-- Every compatible cyclic-algebra element has one unique bounded local coefficient packet. -/
theorem normalForm_hasse_existsUnique (D : CyclicCompanionDatum L)
    (x : CyclicAlgebra D.automorphism (D.predDegree + 1) D.parameter) :
    ∃! f : Fin (D.predDegree + 1) → L,
      cyclicCompanionNormalForm D.automorphism D.predDegree D.parameter f = x := by
  refine ⟨D.normalFormCoordinates x, D.normalForm_reconstruct x, ?_⟩
  intro f hf
  change D.normalFormEquiv f = x at hf
  have h := congrArg D.normalFormEquiv.symm hf
  simpa [normalFormCoordinates] using h

/-- Cyclic-algebra elements agree exactly when every bounded normal-form coefficient agrees. -/
theorem congr_normalFormCoordinate_hasse_iff (D : CyclicCompanionDatum L)
    (x y : CyclicAlgebra D.automorphism (D.predDegree + 1) D.parameter) :
    x = y ↔ ∀ i, D.normalFormCoordinates x i = D.normalFormCoordinates y i := by
  constructor
  · rintro rfl
    exact fun _ ↦ rfl
  · intro h
    apply D.normalFormEquiv.symm.injective
    funext i
    exact h i

/-- A cyclic-algebra element is zero exactly when all normal-form coefficients vanish. -/
theorem eq_zero_normalFormCoordinate_hasse_iff (D : CyclicCompanionDatum L)
    (x : CyclicAlgebra D.automorphism (D.predDegree + 1) D.parameter) :
    x = 0 ↔ ∀ i, D.normalFormCoordinates x i = 0 := by
  rw [D.congr_normalFormCoordinate_hasse_iff]
  simp [normalFormCoordinates]

/-- Every nonzero compatible cyclic-algebra element has a nonzero bounded coefficient. -/
theorem exists_normalFormCoordinate_ne_zero_of_ne_zero
    (D : CyclicCompanionDatum L)
    (x : CyclicAlgebra D.automorphism (D.predDegree + 1) D.parameter)
    (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    ∃ i, D.normalFormCoordinates x i ≠ 0 := by
  by_contra h
  push Not at h
  exact hx ((D.eq_zero_normalFormCoordinate_hasse_iff x).2 h)

end CyclicCompanionDatum
end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ABHN

The first odd prime/Gamma wall--Xi Malgrange residual is strictly negative.  The global
coefficient-generated Stokes--microlocal Witt law has positive terminal and threshold channels
plus one Rees-invariant physical-rank square.  Combining these statements localizes every possible
coefficient-generated realization of the cubic residual to that sole global channel.

More precisely, any landing throughout the nonnegative multi-Rees cone has nonzero common physical
rank, a strictly negative global rank coefficient, rank debt strictly exceeding all positive
microlocal channels, exact negative inertia one, and zero radical.  Thus local microstalk channels
and their Rees deformations cannot carry the missing cubic anomaly.

Conditionally, if one fixed charge lands at both complete threshold contraction and unit Rees scale,
positivity forces every threshold charge to vanish and the landing extends to the entire real
multi-Rees parameter space.  The follow-up diagonal-Rees transversality module uses pendant-cut
faithfulness to prove this fiber empty, so its raw-Euler terminal-energy consequences are vacuous.

This is a classification of every landing charge, not an existence claim for such a charge and not
an RH conclusion.

/-!
# The triangular parameter change

Collecting the pieces: over constants containing a primitive `n`-th root of unity, the tail
coefficients are algebraically independent, they generate the fixed field of the scalings
`p i ↦ ζ ^ i * p i`, the field of rational functions in the parameters is generated over them by the
first parameter alone, and its degree there is exactly `n`, the first parameter being an `n`-th root
of the first tail coefficient.

That is the whole of the parameter change: the coefficient field is a rational function field, and
the parameter field is a Kummer extension of it of degree `n`.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open MvPolynomial

open scoped IntermediateField

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K] {n : ℕ}

omit [CharZero K] in
theorem finite_deckGroup [NeZero n] {ζ : K} (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n) :
    Finite (deckGroup K n) := by
  refine Nat.finite_of_card_ne_zero ?_
  rw [card_deckGroup hζ]
  exact NeZero.ne n

omit [CharZero K] in
theorem card_deckGroup_fintype [NeZero n] {ζ : K} (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n)
    [Fintype (deckGroup K n)] : Fintype.card (deckGroup K n) = n := by
  rw [← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
  exact card_deckGroup hζ

/-- **The coefficient field is the fixed field of the scalings.** -/
theorem tailCoeffField_eq_deckFixedField_of_primitiveRoot (hn : 0 < n) {ζ : K}
    (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n) : tailCoeffField K n = deckFixedField K n := by
  haveI : NeZero n := ⟨by omega⟩
  haveI := finite_deckGroup (K := K) (n := n) hζ
  haveI : Fintype (deckGroup K n) := Fintype.ofFinite _
  exact tailCoeffField_eq_deckFixedField hn (card_deckGroup_fintype hζ)

/-- **The parameter field has degree exactly `n` over the coefficient field.** -/
theorem finrank_tailCoeffField_of_primitiveRoot (hn : 0 < n) {ζ : K}
    (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n) :
    Module.finrank (tailCoeffField K n) (FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K)) = n := by
  haveI : NeZero n := ⟨by omega⟩
  haveI := finite_deckGroup (K := K) (n := n) hζ
  haveI : Fintype (deckGroup K n) := Fintype.ofFinite _
  exact finrank_tailCoeffField hn (card_deckGroup_fintype hζ)

/-- **The triangular parameter change.**  The tail coefficients are algebraically independent, the
parameter field is generated over them by the first parameter, that parameter is an `n`-th root of
the first tail coefficient, and the degree is exactly `n`. -/
theorem tailParameterChange (hn : 0 < n) {ζ : K} (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n) :
    AlgebraicIndependent K (tailCoeff K n) ∧
      (tailCoeffField K n)⟮algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K)
          (FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K)) (MvPolynomial.X (⟨0, hn⟩ : Fin n))⟯ = ⊤ ∧
      (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K) (FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K))
          (MvPolynomial.X (⟨0, hn⟩ : Fin n))) ^ n =
        algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K) (FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K))
          (tailCoeff K n (⟨0, hn⟩ : Fin n)) ∧
      Module.finrank (tailCoeffField K n) (FractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin n) K)) = n :=
  ⟨algebraicIndependent_tailCoeff, tailCoeffField_adjoin_eq_top hn, pow_algebraMap_X_zero hn,
    finrank_tailCoeffField_of_primitiveRoot hn hζ⟩

/-!
# The tail coefficients are linear in the parameter they introduce

The derivative of the `i`-th tail coefficient in the `i`-th parameter is a power of the first
parameter, which no longer involves the `i`-th one.  So subtracting that power times the parameter
leaves something whose derivative in the parameter vanishes, and in characteristic zero that means
the parameter does not occur in it.

Together with the triangularity — the `i`-th coefficient does not involve any later parameter — this
says each tail coefficient is a linear polynomial in the parameter it introduces, with coefficients
in the earlier parameters and leading coefficient a nonzero multiple of a power of the first.  That
is what lets the parameters be solved for one at a time.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open MvPolynomial

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K] {n : ℕ}

/-- The leading coefficient of the `i`-th tail coefficient in the `i`-th parameter. -/
noncomputable def tailLead (K : Type*) [Field K] (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) :
    MvPolynomial (Fin n) K :=
  ((n - (i : ℕ) : ℕ) : MvPolynomial (Fin n) K) *
    (MvPolynomial.X (⟨0, Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.zero_le _) i.2⟩ : Fin n)) ^ (n - (i : ℕ) - 1)

omit [CharZero K] in
theorem pderiv_tailCoeff_self (i : Fin n) :
    MvPolynomial.pderiv i (tailCoeff K n i) = tailLead K n i := by
  have h := tailJacobian_diag (K := K) (n := n) i
  rw [tailJacobian, Matrix.of_apply] at h
  exact h

omit [CharZero K] in
theorem pderiv_tailLead {i j : Fin n} (hj : (j : ℕ) ≠ 0) :
    MvPolynomial.pderiv j (tailLead K n i) = 0 := by
  have hne : (⟨0, Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.zero_le _) i.2⟩ : Fin n) ≠ j := by
    intro hcon
    exact hj (by rw [← hcon])
  have hC : ((n - (i : ℕ) : ℕ) : MvPolynomial (Fin n) K) =
      MvPolynomial.C (((n - (i : ℕ) : ℕ) : K)) := (map_natCast MvPolynomial.C _).symm
  rw [tailLead, hC, Derivation.leibniz, MvPolynomial.pderiv_C, Derivation.leibniz_pow,
    MvPolynomial.pderiv_X_of_ne hne]
  simp

/-- The part of the `i`-th tail coefficient not carrying the `i`-th parameter. -/
noncomputable def tailRemainder (K : Type*) [Field K] (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) :
    MvPolynomial (Fin n) K :=
  tailCoeff K n i - tailLead K n i * MvPolynomial.X i

omit [CharZero K] in
theorem tailCoeff_eq (i : Fin n) :
    tailCoeff K n i = tailLead K n i * MvPolynomial.X i + tailRemainder K n i := by
  rw [tailRemainder]
  ring

omit [CharZero K] in
/-- **The remainder does not involve the parameter, nor any later one.** -/
theorem pderiv_tailRemainder_eq_zero {i j : Fin n} (hi : (i : ℕ) ≠ 0) (hij : (i : ℕ) ≤ (j : ℕ)) :
    MvPolynomial.pderiv j (tailRemainder K n i) = 0 := by
  have hj0 : (j : ℕ) ≠ 0 := by omega
  have hcoeff : MvPolynomial.pderiv j (tailCoeff K n i) =
      if (i : ℕ) = (j : ℕ) then tailLead K n i else 0 := by
    by_cases hij' : (i : ℕ) = (j : ℕ)
    · rw [if_pos hij']
      have : i = j := Fin.ext hij'
      rw [← this, pderiv_tailCoeff_self]
    · rw [if_neg hij']
      have hlt : i < j := by
        refine Fin.lt_def.2 ?_
        omega
      have h := tailJacobian_upperTriangular (K := K) (n := n) (i := j) (j := i) hlt
      rw [tailJacobian, Matrix.of_apply] at h
      exact h
  rw [tailRemainder, map_sub, hcoeff, Derivation.leibniz, pderiv_tailLead hj0]
  by_cases hij' : (i : ℕ) = (j : ℕ)
  · have hie : i = j := Fin.ext hij'
    rw [if_pos hij', ← hie, MvPolynomial.pderiv_X_self]
    simp
  · rw [if_neg hij']
    have hne : i ≠ j := fun hcon => hij' (by rw [hcon])
    rw [MvPolynomial.pderiv_X_of_ne hne]
    simp

/-- **The remainder is free of the parameter and of every later one.** -/
theorem degreeOf_tailRemainder_eq_zero {i j : Fin n} (hi : (i : ℕ) ≠ 0) (hij : (i : ℕ) ≤ (j : ℕ)) :
    (tailRemainder K n i).degreeOf j = 0 :=
  degreeOf_eq_zero_of_pderiv_eq_zero (pderiv_tailRemainder_eq_zero hi hij)

omit [CharZero K] in
/-- **The first tail coefficient is a power of the first parameter.** -/
theorem tailCoeff_zero (hn : 0 < n) :
    tailCoeff K n (⟨0, hn⟩ : Fin n) = MvPolynomial.X (⟨0, hn⟩ : Fin n) ^ n := by
  rw [tailCoeff]
  simpa using coeff_zero_tailPoly_pow (K := K) (n := n) hn n

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-!
# Complex spectral-coefficient laws on real parameter spaces

Hermitian matrix families have complex polynomial entries but real control
parameters.  This file pulls the universal unordered spectral-relation
polynomials through complex characteristic-coefficient families and proves
one-witness residual full-measure genericity on the real parameter space.
-/

open Set Topology MeasureTheory

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- Pull one universal unordered spectral-relation obstruction through a
complex-polynomial characteristic-coefficient family. -/
def complexSpectralCoefficientObstructionPullback
    {θ I : Type*} [Fintype I]
